chunks: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:

'I will be the first delegate to the Mighty, the Compeller, on the Day of Resurrection — and (also) His Book and the People of my Household. Then (will come) my community. Then I will ask them: What did you do with the Book of God and with the People of my Household?'

key_terms.أَهْلُ بَيْتِي: The People of my Household (Ahl al-Bayt) — the Prophet's family, specifically Imam Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn and their descendants, the Imams. In Shia theology, guardianship of the Quran and the imamate are vested in them.
key_terms.أُمَّتِي: My community/nation (umma) — the Muslim community as a whole, who will be questioned for their stewardship of the two trusts.
key_terms.الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ: Two of the names of God — al-'Aziz (the Mighty/Invincible) and al-Jabbar (the Compeller/All-Powerful). Their use here emphasizes divine authority and dominion on Judgment Day.
key_terms.وَافِدٍ: Delegate or emissary; one who arrives as a representative before a higher authority. Here indicating the Prophet's privileged intercessory role on the Day of Judgment.

ai.seo_question: What will the Prophet ask his community on the Day of Judgment about the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) transmits a hadith of the Prophet (SAWW) declaring that on the Day of Resurrection, he will be the first to appear before God Almighty, accompanied by the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt, followed by his community. The Prophet will then hold his community accountable for how they treated the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt — the two things he left behind as the Thaqalayn (two weighty things). This hadith is a direct statement of eschatological accountability, emphasizing that the community's treatment of the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt will be the measure by which they are judged.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud who said, 
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said:

‘I<sup>saww</sup> would be the first delegate to the Mighty, the Compeller, on the Day of Judgment, and (and so would be) His<sup>azwj</sup> Book, and the People<sup>asws</sup> of my<sup>saww</sup> Household. Then it would be my<sup>saww</sup> community, then I<sup>saww</sup> would ask them what they did with the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and with the People<sup>asws</sup> of my<sup>saww</sup> Household’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from abu al-Jarud who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said that the Messenger of Allah has said, ‘

I will be the first to arrive before the Majestic, the Almighty on the Day of Judgment, His book and my family, then my followers whom I will ask about what they have done to the book of Allah and my family.’”
